title: Heaviest Strictly Rising Run
statement:
You get an array nums of positive integers. A rising run is a contiguous piece of the array in which every value is strictly greater than the one before it. A single element is a rising run on its own.

Return the largest sum of any rising run.

examples.why: The run [2, 3, 5, 6] sums to 16. The run [4, 9] is shorter but only reaches 13.
Equal neighbours break a run, because the rise must be strict. Each 2 stands alone.
The run [1, 2, 3, 50] sums to 56. The 4 after the 50 starts a new run.

hints: Every rising run ends somewhere. If you knew the best run ending at index i−1, what is the best run ending at i?
A run can only continue when nums[i] is strictly bigger than nums[i−1]. Otherwise a new run starts at i.
Keep a running sum of the current run. Add to it while the values rise, reset it to nums[i] when they don't, and track the largest value it ever reaches.

explain.intuition:
The rising runs split the array into separate pieces: each place where nums[i] ≤ nums[i − 1] is a cut. Since every value is positive, the best run inside a piece is the whole piece, so the answer is simply the heaviest piece.

That means one pass is enough. Keep the sum of the current piece. When the next value rises, add it; when it does not, close the piece and start a new one at the current value. It is a window that only grows on the right and jumps its left edge to i at a cut.
steps: For each i from 1: if nums[i] > nums[i − 1], add nums[i] to cur; otherwise set cur = nums[i].
After each step, set best = max(best, cur).
pitfalls: Using >= instead of >. Equal neighbours must end a run, as in [1, 2, 2, 3, 4].
Updating best only when a run breaks, which misses a run that reaches the end of the array.
Resetting cur to 0 instead of nums[i], which drops the first value of the new run.

solutions.title: Extend every start
solutions.idea: From each start index, walk right while the values keep rising and record the sum.

solutions.title: One pass with a running sum
solutions.idea: Extend the current run while values rise, restart it at every non-rise, and keep the best sum seen.

followups: Values may now be negative. Is the whole piece still the best run inside it? What changes?
Return the start and end index of the heaviest run, choosing the earliest one on ties.
